react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR = 1.43×10⁻¹¹), MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (p = 3.25×10⁻⁷), and Mummichog m/z-direct network activity (p = 0.027) — converge on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00052 / SMPDB:SMP00043) as the dominant affected pathway. Four driver metabolites drove this consensus: sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), galactinol (KEGG:C01235, α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol), and myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137). All four appear in the Leloir pathway member rosters from both the RaMP and MetaboAnalystR EnrichmentResults. Mummichog independently confirmed the galactose cluster via 10 empirical network hits and additionally surfaced Glycerophospholipid metabolism (MUMM pathway, p = 0.0249) through myo-inositol and the lipid-derived mediator 16(R)-HETE (KEGG:C14778). D-glucose (KEGG:C00221) contributed to Mummichog's Hexose Phosphorylation (p = 0.0029) and Glycerophospholipid hits, reflecting its dual role as both a galactose precursor and an upstream hexose. Beta-alanine (KEGG:C00099) appeared in lower-ranked ORA hits (three KEGG pathways, p ≈ 0.06–0.07) but did not achieve cross-paradigm significance. The convergent signal across ORA and network-diffusion tools strengthens the biological interpretation of a coordinated perturbation of galactose sugar metabolism and, to a lesser extent, inositol-mediated phospholipid signaling under the treatment condition.

  "narrative_text": "Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in the treatment group. Mummichog m/z-direct network activity independently confirms the galactose cluster, placing Hexose Phosphorylation (MUMM:hexose_phosphorylation) at rank 1 with p = 0.0027, and Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism) at rank 4 with p = 0.011. The four driver metabolites are sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and galactinol (KEGG:C01235). Galactinol is the most pathway-specific driver because it is synthesized exclusively through the galactose metabolism network. D-glucose (KEGG:C00221) is the upstream hexose that feeds into this cluster via Mummichog Hexose Phosphorylation. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) returns Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) both at FDR = 1.43×10⁻¹¹, with the same four metabolites hitting: sucrose, galactitol, myo-inositol, and galactinol. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently returns hsa00052 (KEGG:hsa00052) with p = 3.25×10⁻⁷, again hitting sucrose, galactitol, myo-inositol, and galactinol. Mummichog m/z-direct network activity independently confirms the galactose cluster, placing Hexose Phosphorylation (MUMM:hexose_phosphorylation) at rank 1 with p = 0.0027, and Starch and Sucrose Metabolism (MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism) at rank 4 with p = 0.011. The four driver metabolites are sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and galactinol (KEGG:C01235).
